delta: The lore regex key fix (slice 4 `lore-templates-and-tokens`, implementation plan owner answer 10)
before: ../lore-regex.json (captured at efad2b76, the browser path before the fix)
fixed: shared/lore/activation.ts, `searchMatch`, the `arg.regex` branch (the client's `loadLoreBookV3Prompt` wraps it)
semantics: A key `/pattern/flags` splits at its last `/`: the pattern is between the first and the last slash, the flags follow the last slash. Before, `split('/').pop()` took the flags and the key was rewritten to `'/' + pattern` (the leading slash stayed in the pattern), so `/dragon/i` matched only a literal `/dragon`.
Empty flags are allowed: `/dragon/` is the pattern `dragon` with no flags. Before, the empty flags string was falsy and the key was skipped, so it never matched.

No key is rewritten in place. Before, the rewritten key landed in `arg.keys[0]`, so the second scanned message was tested with `/dragon`, whose 'flags' were then the pattern text; `new RegExp('', 'dragon')` threw and the search ended with no match.

`matchLog.activated` is the key as written (the key is no longer rewritten; it was the original string before the fix too). The `prompt` and `source` rows are built as before: a user message under the scanned user name, a character message under `msg.name`, the speaker, or the character's name.
unchanged: i-flag-slash-in-text: `Take the /dragon path.` contains `dragon`, so `/dragon/i` matches it after the fix as the literal `/dragon` did before; same active, same log row.
i-flag-two-messages-match-first: the match is in the first scanned message, before the rewrite could break the second scan; same active, same log row.
two-keys-second-matches: `/cat/i` does not match, `/dragon/i` matches `Take the /dragon path.` after the fix as the literal `/dragon` did before; same active, same log row.
plain-key-control: a plain key is not a regex key; untouched by the fix.

i-flag-plain-text.change: `/dragon/i` now activates `regex-i` on `A dragon appears.`; before, nothing activated.
i-flag-plain-text.why: The pattern is `dragon` with the flag `i` (split at the last `/`), and `dragon` is in the text. Before, the key was rewritten to `/dragon`, which the text does not contain.

empty-flags-plain-text.change: `/dragon/` now activates `regex-empty` on `A dragon appears.`; before, nothing activated.
empty-flags-plain-text.why: Empty flags are allowed: the pattern is `dragon` with no flags, and `dragon` is in the text. Before, the empty flags string was falsy and the key was never tested.

i-flag-two-messages-match-second.change: `/dragon/i` now activates `regex-i` from the second scanned message (`Take the /dragon path.`, by the character); before, nothing activated.
i-flag-two-messages-match-second.why: `Hello there.` (message 0) does not match, and the key is no longer rewritten after that test, so message 1 is tested with the same `/dragon/i` and matches. Before, message 1 was tested with the rewritten `/dragon`, whose 'flags' were `dragon`, which threw and ended the search. The log row is the character message's: `{{Regex}}` is the character's name (no `msg.name`, no speaker), `message 1 by char` is its index and role.
